question: How often does the unchanged BC-013 nominal pointwise gain contour include its generating gain on new synthetic noise realizations?

design.noise: Fresh independent numpy default_rng(seed) Gaussian draws at all 241 times and three channels; multiply by unchanged BC-013 SD [5,10,30]; set t=0 glucose and insulin errors exactly zero; reuse each interior draw across its three observation designs. No BC-013 development seed is reused.
design.reference: Generate each case's noiseless trajectory from the unchanged BC-012 reference solver at its declared truth. Exact basal G/I and known SC input remain conditioned; t=0 C-peptide remains observed.
design.sampling: Unchanged 30-minute BC-013 observation selection over 0-240 minutes: 25 GIC or 16 GI residuals. No participant or human measurement is used.

analysis.method: For each new dataset, minimize unchanged BC-013 Q freely with its three fixed starts and with the generating gain fixed using the same two deterministic nuisance starts. DeltaQ is constrained minus unrestricted Q; never clip negative values. A true gain is included when DeltaQ <= 3.841458820694124.
analysis.optimizer: Unchanged BC-013 bounds, log-coordinate trust-region solver, fixed SD, analytic nuisance-volume projection, starts and finite-difference step. The BC-013 protocol is adapted only to name each new dataset assessment; no inference rule or model equation changes.
analysis.solver_check: Evaluate every fit-solver selected optimum with the reference forward solver. Compare each Q and DeltaQ to the fit solver within 0.001. If a fitted DeltaQ lies within 0.01 of the cutoff or the solver evaluations disagree on inclusion, rerun both unrestricted and constrained optimizations with the reference solver. Unresolved disagreement is a numerical failure.
analysis.outcome: Primary conservative coverage is included/number planned, counting any incomplete or failed replicate as noncoverage and reporting that count separately. Also show included/number completed as a diagnostic, never as a replacement primary denominator.
analysis.uncertainty: Report two-sided 95% Wilson score intervals for each planned-denominator proportion. At nominal p=0.95, n=64 has binomial Monte Carlo SE about 0.027 and an approximate normal 95% half-width about 0.053; n=32 has SE about 0.039. Report observed Wilson intervals even if coverage differs. These sample sizes cannot prove exact 95% calibration.
analysis.comparison: The three interior observation designs use paired noise draws but their marginal pointwise coverages are reported separately; no independent-group test or superiority claim. The gain-boundary case is a diagnostic under nonregular conditions, not a nominal 95% calibration target.
analysis.calibration: No threshold tuning is permitted in this assessment. Any future calibration needs separate noise realizations and a new frozen assessment set.

execution.repeat: Execute the complete campaign twice in separate processes from the same frozen protocol and seeds; require byte-identical observation and case artifacts. Retain all starts, failures, solver checks, truth, observations, source snapshots and environment locks.
execution.artifacts: Failure-aware manifest; one observation file per generating case/seed; one fit file per case/seed/design in each run; standard-library arithmetic and completeness reconstruction; aggregate JSON and deterministic SVG. No raw health data.
execution.acceptance: All planned replicates must complete with all declared starts, finite model/optimizer outputs, constrained Q no more than 0.0001 below unrestricted Q, reference objective/DeltaQ agreement within 0.001, exact numeric repeat, and reconstructible denominator, Wilson interval and figure. The empirical coverage value is a finding, not an acceptance gate.

limitations: One fixed synthetic patient and unchanged 24-state model; no human or T1D population calibration
Known exact basal glucose/insulin and SC input; fixed hepatic, action, meal and C-peptide exchange assumptions
Only evoked gain is assessed; no joint coverage or other parameter coverage claim
Three starts and bounded nuisance optimization cannot prove global minima
One reference-solver check per chosen fit does not establish global solver equivalence
Finite Monte Carlo precision and an engineering parameter box
Boundary diagnostics do not validate the asymptotic chi-square cutoff
No threshold calibration, therapy effect, beta-cell count or clinical recommendation

sources.use: weighted Gaussian likelihood and nuisance-reoptimized pointwise profile region
